name: OpenFlexure Microscope
author: OpenFlexure (Richard Bowman, Julian Stirling a kol.)
alt: Tištěný mikroskop OpenFlexure na stojanu se zásuvkou na elektroniku, s krokovými motory a osvětlením nad stolkem
short: Tištěný mikroskop, jehož stolek se posouvá na ohebných plastových kloubech. Tři krokové motory, objektiv RMS a kamera Raspberry Pi.
lead: Otevřený mikroskop s posuvem ve třech osách. Tělo se stolkem se tiskne vcelku a stolek se posouvá na ohebných plastových kloubech (flexurách); podle autorů tak dosahuje velmi jemného posuvu v rozsahu asi 10 mm. Každou osu posouvá šroub M3 v mosazné matici; šroubem otáčí krokový motor 28BYJ-48 přes ozubená kola s převodem 2 : 1 (existuje i ruční verze s kolečky). Motory řídí deska Sangaboard, obraz snímá kamera Raspberry Pi Camera v2 a Raspberry Pi 4 je v zásuvce ve stojanu. Model ukazuje motorizovanou verzi s objektivem RMS a tubusovou čočkou; levnější verze používá místo objektivu čočku z kamery Pi. Shora vzorek osvětluje deska s LED přes difuzor a kondenzor. Model vychází z vývojové verze v7.0.0-beta5. Mikroskop se ovládá softwarem autorů OpenFlexure server s webovým rozhraním, který běží na Raspberry Pi.

en.credit: Render from the OpenFlexure Microscope v7 OpenSCAD sources (CERN-OHL-S-2.0): motorised version with an RMS objective. We placed the parts with the positions from the authors’ render scripts; we placed the motors, Raspberry Pi and Sangaboard ourselves from the mounting lugs and the drawer in the design. Screws, nuts, bands, cables, lenses, the LED board and the diffuser are not modelled.
en.author: OpenFlexure (Richard Bowman, Julian Stirling et al.)
en.alt: Printed OpenFlexure microscope on a stand with an electronics drawer, with stepper motors and illumination above the stage
en.short: Printed microscope whose stage moves on flexible plastic hinges. Three stepper motors, an RMS objective and a Raspberry Pi camera.
en.lead: An open microscope with three-axis motion. The body with its stage is printed in one piece and the stage moves on flexible plastic hinges (flexures); according to the authors this gives very fine motion over a range of about 10 mm. Each axis is moved by an M3 screw in a brass nut; a 28BYJ-48 stepper motor turns the screw through 2 : 1 gears (there is also a manual version with thumbwheels). A Sangaboard drives the motors, a Raspberry Pi Camera v2 takes the image and a Raspberry Pi 4 sits in a drawer in the stand. The model shows the motorised version with an RMS objective and a tube lens; the lower-cost version uses the Pi camera’s own lens instead of an objective. An LED board lights the sample from above through a diffuser and a condenser. The model is based on the development version v7.0.0-beta5. The microscope is controlled by the authors’ OpenFlexure server software with a web interface, running on the Raspberry Pi.
en.software: The microscope is controlled by the authors’ OpenFlexure server with a web interface on the Raspberry Pi (GPL-3.0)
